✅ My security checklist

    Keep practicing for free
    • Mass.gov: official Commonwealth services
    • Boston Public Library: free help and classes
    • Tech Goes Home: digital skills for Boston residents
    • DigitalLearn: free video lessons
    • Applied Digital Skills from Google
    • Senior Planet: classes for people 60+
    • Northstar: check your skills
    These open real websites outside this practice space.
    ♿ Accessibility help
    • Keyboard: press Tab to move, Enter or Space to choose. Everything works without a mouse.
    • Screen reader: turn “Room view” off. Rooms and scenes are described in text, and each screen is announced.
    • Deaf or hard of hearing: nothing depends on sound. Every step appears as written captions. Turn on “Large captions” inside a scene, or open “Text version of this lesson”.
    • Low vision: use A+ for bigger text and High contrast.
    • Feel it: on phones and tablets that can vibrate, taps buzz (short for a tap, double for correct, long for not yet). “Sound cues” adds soft tones for blind learners. On every device the on-screen keyboard and trackpad press down when you act.
    • Low sound sensitivity: “Read aloud” is optional and off by default.
    🤝 Running a free community session
    1. Welcome. Explain that everything is fictional and nothing is collected.
    2. Watch one scene together on a screen, with captions on.
    3. Learners try along in pairs. Pair a sighted learner with a screen-reader user if you can.
    4. Discuss “Have you ever seen this kind of scam?”
    5. Fill in the safety card below and take it home.

    This space is free, needs no sign-in, and works on a Chromebook, phone or laptop.

    📇 My safety card

    My Safety Card

    1. Pause. Scams hurry you.
    2. Verify. Call back on a number you already have.
    3. Never pay with gift cards, wire or crypto.
    4. Never share a texted code or password.
    5. Voices and videos can be faked by AI.
    6. Being tricked is not your fault. Tell someone and act fast.

        📘 For learning only. Made-up data, nothing collected. Read more
        This lab is a training space. It is not connected to any real service, store, hospital or agency, and it never sends your information anywhere. The people, accounts, phone numbers, amounts and practice websites in these scenes are made up (synthetic data). Real agency names such as Mass.gov, the RMV and MassHealth appear so you know what to look for, but nothing here connects to them. Rules and forms change, so always confirm on mass.gov or by calling 2‑1‑1. The only real people named are the historical figures honored on the lamp tables. Nothing you do here is real, and nothing is collected. Examples use Roxbury, Massachusetts, USA. Agencies, phone numbers and programmes differ from place to place, so treat them as models and add the trusted help in your own area.
